newsitem.title: UK: Skyepharma slides 13 pct on funding news.
newsitem.headline: Skyepharma slides 13 pct on funding news.

text.p: Shares in British-based drug technology company SkyePharma Plc slid 12.5 percent on Thursday after the company said it would seek further funding to cover additional investment and a 12-month delay in developing two diabetes drugs.

Sources close to the company said it was considering an ADR issue in the U.S. together with a rights issue or placing in Britain to help cover a consequent one-year setback in its projected profitability.
The shortfall is thought to be around 20 million pounds.
Shares in the company closed down 11 pence at 76 1/2 pence.

SkyePharma is creating new ways of administering drugs, including slow release tablets, for a number of leading pharmaceutical companies. It is also developing its own pipeline of generic products through its U.S. subsidiary, Brightstone Pharma Inc.

The company said expansion of its own portfolio of generic drugs under development, the acquisition of further manufacturing capacity in France and investment in respiratory drugs had all led to increased spending.

Skyepharma said it was also delaying generic versions of two diabetic drugs, Glipizide and Glyburide, by a year because of capacity constraints at its Jago subsidiary in Switzerland. It said it would give priority to drugs being developed for other companies, which were all on schedule.
The company's brokers, SBC Warburg, said they had changed their forecast for 1998 to a loss of 16 million stg from a pre-tax profit of 6.8 million stg.
For 1999 the forecast has been amended to a pre-tax profit of 58.2 million stg compared with a previous estimate of 65 million stg.
